verdict.summary: MARA is an industrial bitcoin producer with treasury leverage, not an AI data-center company in current reported economics. Q2 revenue fell 27% YoY to $174.9 million despite 70.3 EH/s energized hashrate, because mining economics remained exposed to network difficulty, power cost and bitcoin price. Production improved 3% YoY to 2,422 BTC, but purchased-energy cost per coin rose 14.7% to $38,690 and GAAP net loss reached $611.3 million, including a $343 million bitcoin fair-value loss. The balance sheet carried 35,577 BTC and $421.3 million cash, yet $2.47 billion of debt and a subsequent $600 million BTC-backed facility increase common-equity convexity. Long Ridge and Matagorda create credible power-site optionality for AI/HPC, but neither is a contracted AI revenue stream in the quarter. A D+ quality grade is therefore appropriate: scale and assets are real, earnings quality and leverage are weak. The current trade remains watch-only until $11.60 confirms; bitcoin rallies cannot substitute for improving cost per hash and financing discipline.

business.overview:
MARA earns current revenue by operating bitcoin-mining fleets: realized BTC price, coins produced, network difficulty, fleet efficiency and power cost determine gross economics. Q2 production was 2,422 BTC from 70.3 EH/s energized hashrate, but revenue still fell because capacity did not offset weaker price-volume economics. It sold 2,213 BTC at an average $73,078, making treasury-sale policy another cash-flow variable.

The AI transmission channel is physical power infrastructure. Long Ridge and prospective Matagorda capacity could host HPC loads, but conversion requires interconnection, cooling, customer contracts, construction capital and service-level reliability; no Q2 AI revenue was reported and no site right should be modeled as rent.

The model breaks when hashprice falls below fleet-and-power cost, collateralized BTC declines, curtailment or interconnection delays reduce utilization, or debt-funded expansion fails to produce per-share cash flow. Treasury appreciation can mask weak mining unit economics temporarily, while pledged coins become less available precisely when financing tightens.
business.moat: MARA's advantage is scale, site-development capability and access to energy assets, not proprietary bitcoin economics. Its 70.3 EH/s fleet spreads overhead, while Long Ridge and Matagorda may create differentiated power inventory; network difficulty and commodity hardware keep the core moat narrow.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 revenue was $174.9M, down 27% YoY from $238.5M. MARA produced 2,422 BTC, up 3% YoY, while energized hashrate rose 22% to 70.3 EH/s; purchased-energy cost per BTC increased 14.7% to $38,690. A $343M BTC fair-value loss helped drive the GAAP result to a $611.3M net loss, or -$1.60 per share. The separate non-GAAP bridge ended at -$360.9M of adjusted EBITDA. No annual revenue or EPS guidance was issued; the principal caveat is that BTC accounting and treasury sales can dominate mining operating trends.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: MARA's 386.3M basic-share snapshot sits behind $2.47B of debt. The Q2 10-Q identifies 82,691,847 anti-dilutive potential shares: 12,385,624 RSUs, 20,950,294 performance RSUs at maximum vesting and 49,355,929 convertible-note shares. Adding them gives a 468.992M minimum dilution sensitivity, not a current GAAP diluted count because vesting and conversion conditions remain conditional. After quarter-end, two $300M bitcoin-backed facilities were initially collateralized by 18,750 BTC; they are secured debt, not equity issuance or the separate up-to-$600M Matagorda milestone consideration.

filingsReview.summary: 3 decision-relevant primary filing(s) are displayed with accession-specific findings. Grade D+ measures fundamentals; trade state watch measures timing and is evaluated separately.

filings.finding: The Q2 10-Q supports $421.3M cash, $2.47B debt and 35,577 BTC, and discloses two post-quarter $300M bitcoin-backed facilities initially collateralized by 18,750 BTC: Coinbase at federal-funds midpoint plus 3.875% and Two Prime at fixed 7.65%. This is secured debt, not equity issuance or the separate Matagorda consideration.
The August 6 8-K furnishes the shareholder letter reporting $174.9M revenue, 2,422 BTC produced, -$360.9M non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA and subsequent $600M BTC-backed acquisition debt facilities.
The 2025 10-K establishes mining, power, network-difficulty, custody and debt risks plus the annual control baseline; it does not support treating prospective HPC sites as contracted revenue.

contrarianRisks: The $600M BTC-backed facilities are debt, not an equity sale, but collateral and interest make them economically consequential.
9,270 BTC were loaned or pledged; total holdings overstate freely deployable liquidity.
AI/HPC site rights and acquisitions do not equal contracted revenue or conversion economics.
BTC fair-value losses are non-operating but economically relevant to a treasury-heavy balance sheet.
Hashrate growth can destroy value when difficulty and power cost rise faster than BTC output.

risks.riskSummary: MARA combines deteriorating mining revenue with treasury and collateral leverage; negative adjusted EBITDA, pledged bitcoin and debt-funded site expansion can reinforce one another during a BTC drawdown, while the AI option remains too early to provide an operating offset. Retail war-room: model a BTC or collateral headline gap through $10.93, route limits during regular-session liquidity because miner spreads and slippage expand at the open, size for the full $0.67 risk, avoid financing and earnings events, and never chase above the $11.60 activation; $12.76 is the first planned exit at about 1.73R.
